react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites revealed two interconnected metabolic modules driven by one-carbon metabolism. The dominant signal is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260), which achieved rank 1 in RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR=8.59×10⁻¹⁷, fold enrichment=737) and rank 1 in mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.0018, 8/8 input metabolites overlapped). The second coherent cluster is Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270, FDR=1.05×10⁻¹⁴) and its WikiPathways catabolism view Cysteine and methionine catabolism (WP:WP4504, FDR=3.03×10⁻¹²), confirmed by mummichog at rank 2 (p=0.007). Seven of the ten input metabolites are verified pathway members via enrichment hit-rosters: glycine (C00037), L-serine (C00065), L-threonine (C00188), L-cysteine (C00097), choline (C00114), adenosine (C00212), and S-adenosylmethionine (C00019, SAM). SAM is the central one-carbon donor linking both clusters; its differential abundance drives methylation capacity and transsulfuration pathway flux. L-2-Amino-3-oxobutanoic acid (C03508, also called 2-amino-3-oxobutanoate) is a downstream cystathionine β-synthase substrate that bridges methionine→cysteine conversion, consistent with the cystathionine β-synthase deficiency disease-signatures hit in SMPDB. 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) appeared in tyrosine metabolism (mummichog p=0.043) as a peripheral signal. Sucrose (C00089) did not enrich in the primary amino-acid pathways. The cross-paradigm consensus strongly implicates perturbed one-carbon/methyl-group metabolism and transsulfuration as the biological story.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-database over-representation analysis (RaMP) identified Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the top pathway with FDR 8.59×10⁻¹⁷ and 7 of 10 input metabolites mapped. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranked Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) as the top hit with p-value 0.0021, confirming cross-paradigm consensus on this amino-acid hub. The verified driver metabolites are glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-serine (KEGG:C00065), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), choline (KEGG:C00114), adenosine (KEGG:C00212), and S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019) — all documented members of the RaMP KEGG:map00260 metabolite roster. S-adenosylmethionine links the amino-acid cluster to methyl-group transfer reactions; its differential abundance is consistent with perturbed one-carbon metabolism. L-2-amino-3-oxobutanoic acid (KEGG:C03508) did not enrich in the primary amino-acid pathway, and sucrose (KEGG:C00089) was not mapped to any significant hit. The biological story centers on coordinated perturbation of glycine-serine-threonine metabolism across two independent enrichment paradigms.
